import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Green's Open Problem 85

*Carbery’s rectangle problem*

References:
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.85)
- [CCW99] Carbery, Anthony, Michael Christ, and James Wright. "Multidimensional van der Corput and sublevel set estimates." Journal of the American Mathematical Society 12.4 (1999): 981-1015 Section 6.
- [Ke00] Keleti, Tamás. "Density and covering properties of intervals of ℝn." Mathematika 47.1-2 (2000): 229-242.
- [KKM02] Katz, Nets Hawk, Elliot Krop, and Mauro Maggioni. "Remarks on the box problem." Mathematical Research Letters 9.4 (2002): 515-520.
- [Mu02] Mubayi, Dhruv. "Some exact results and new asymptotics for hypergraph Turán numbers." Combinatorics, Probability and Computing 11.3 (2002): 299-309 Conjecture 1.4.
- [CPZ20] Conlon, David, Cosmin Pohoata, and Dmitriy Zakharov. "Random multilinear maps and the Erd\H {o} s box problem." arXiv preprint arXiv:2011.09024 (2020).
-/

open Filter MeasureTheory Set Topology

namespace Green85

/--
Suppose that $A$ is an open subset of $[0, 1]^2$ with measure $\alpha$. Are there four points in
$A$ determining an axis-parallel rectangle with area $\gt c \alpha^2$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 28 52]
theorem green_85 :
  answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c > 0, ∀ A : Set (ℝ × ℝ),
    IsOpen A →
    A ⊆ Icc 0 1 ×ˢ Icc 0 1 →
    A.Nonempty →
    let α := (volume A).toReal
    ∃ x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂,
      {(x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₁), (x₂, y₂), (x₁, y₂)} ⊆ A ∧
      c * α ^ 2 ≤ |x₁ - x₂| * |y₁ - y₂| := by
  sorry

/--
From [Gr24] "It is quite easy to show using Cauchy-Schwarz that there must be such a rectangle with
area $\gg \alpha^2 (\log 1/\alpha)^{-1}$."
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 28 52]
theorem green_85_loose :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ α in 𝓝[>] 0,
    ∀ A : Set (ℝ × ℝ),
    IsOpen A →
    A ⊆ Icc 0 1 ×ˢ Icc 0 1 →
    A.Nonempty →
    α = (volume A).toReal →
    ∃ x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂,
      {(x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₁), (x₂, y₂), (x₁, y₂)} ⊆ A ∧
      c * α ^ 2 * (Real.log (1/α))⁻¹ ≤ |x₁ - x₂| * |y₁ - y₂| := by
  sorry

end Green85

findings.description: The module bibliography gives the page range of [KKM02], “Remarks on the box problem,” as 515–520. The published article spans 515–519. This is only a bibliographic error; neither theorem is affected.
findings.source_evidence: The published PDF begins “Mathematical Research Letters 9, 515–519 (2002)” and ends on page 519: https://intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/mrl/2002/0009/0004/MRL-2002-0009-0004-a011.pdf. Green’s bibliography, reference [188], also gives 515–519.
findings.suggested_fix: In the [KKM02] reference on line 28, replace “515-520” with “515-519”.

reformulations.difference: Positive measure and four distinct vertices are implicit: Lean assumes A.Nonempty and uses a set literal of four corner expressions, without separate coordinate-distinctness hypotheses.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For an open nonempty subset of the unit square, Lebesgue measure is positive and at most 1. Thus α = (volume A).toReal is genuinely positive and finite. With c > 0, the area inequality forces |x₁−x₂|·|y₁−y₂| > 0, hence both coordinates differ and the four vertices are distinct. Conversely, an explicit positive-measure, distinct-vertex formulation implies the Lean formulation. This equivalence was proved as main_iff_distinct in scratch.lean. The docstring’s strict area inequality is also equivalent to Lean’s weak inequality by replacing c with c/2; main_iff_strict verifies this.

reformulations.difference: For Green’s class of open unit-square sets, Lean states the logarithmic bound only eventually as α → 0⁺. The primary paper’s Proposition 6.1 gives an all-density bound using log⁺(u) = max(1, log u).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The right-neighborhood quantifier means there is δ > 0 such that the bound holds uniformly for every 0 < α < δ. Choose 0 < t < 1 with t² < δ and apply it to tA. Measure and rectangle area scale by t², giving a rectangle in A of area at least c·t²·α²/(log(1/α)+log(1/t²)). Since 0 < α ≤ 1, this implies the all-density bound with denominator max(1,log(1/α)) and constant c·t²/(1+log(1/t²)). Conversely, for α < exp(−1), the truncated logarithm equals the ordinary logarithm. Both the filter interpretation and the full equivalence for the same open-set class were proved in Lean as loose_iff_small_density and loose_iff_logplus.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalizations were found in either theorem. The cited Green survey still presents the quadratic bound as open and the logarithmically weaker bound as known, agreeing with both category tags. Checks covered answer scope, quantifier uniformity, positive finite measure, nondegenerate rectangles, realizability of every small positive density, and logarithm/filter boundary cases. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully; the equivalence proofs have no sorry dependencies. Keleti’s full text was unavailable, but Green and Carbery–Christ–Wright directly settle the faithfulness of both declarations. The reviewed file remains byte-for-byte identical to the committed version.
